messages.subject: Fixing Ability to Zero
parts:
Hi Phil

Thanks in advance for your help and the great opportunity to dicuss questions in this forum. I am conducting a bifactor IRT. Regarding Toland et al.'s approach (2017), I want to compute a bifactor GR model where the trait abilities or θiS, respectively, are fixed to zero in order to get a conditional item category characteristic curve for each of the items. Can you share a possibility to do this within the MIRT package?

Kind regards,
Mathias

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fixing Ability to Zero
parts:
Hi Mathias,

Isn't fixing conditioning on all specific factors @ 0 equivalent to plotting just the uni-dimensional dimension? This is easily accomplished by just creating a new, temporary model, whereby the general factor slopes and intercepts are extracted from the bifactor model and used as the uni-dimensional model's slope-intercept combination. There's many ways to create models with fixed parameters in the mirt-package forum, but feel free to ask if you run into difficulties extracting and creating this submodel. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Fixing Ability to Zero
parts:
On Fri, Nov 23, 2018 at 11:44 AM <mathias....@gmail.com> wrote:
Plotting the estimates for the bifactor sounds reasonable. Even if I might be wrong: to my understanding Toland et al. fixed the trait abilities within the model.

If they fix the traits to 0 then these effectively drop out of the model. Anything times 0 is 0, so the equation

P(y = k) = logit(a1 * theta1 + a2 * theta2 + .... + ak * thetak + d)

would simplify to 

P(y = k) = logit(a1 * theta1 + d)  

if all theta2 to thetak = 0. There's no difference in interpretation.

I neither found a possibility to only extract the bifactor parameters nor found a possibility to fix the ability to zero. Sorry if I am asking a basic R question in case of plotting just the bifactor. However, I need some help for fixing the abiltiy for the specific factors. Could you help with both aspects?

Here's an example.

####
library(mirt)
data(SAT12)
data <- key2binary(SAT12,
                   key = c(1,4,5,2,3,1,2,1,3,1,2,4,2,1,5,3,4,4,1,4,3,3,4,1,3,5,1,3,1,5,4,5))
specific <- c(2,3,2,3,3,2,1,2,1,1,1,3,1,3,1,2,1,1,3,3,1,1,3,1,3,3,1,3,2,3,1,2)
mod1 <- bfactor(data, specific)
cfs <- coef(mod1, simplify=TRUE)$items

general_slopes <- cfs[,'a1']
intercepts <- cfs[,'d']

sv <- mirt(data, 1, pars='values')
sv$est <- FALSE
sv$value[sv$name == 'a1'] <- general_slopes
sv$value[sv$name == 'd'] <- intercepts

unidim <- mirt(data, 1, pars = sv)
coef(unidim, simplify=TRUE)

plot(unidim, type = 'trace')

####

Many thanks in advance.

Mathias
